entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes' (dated 26 September 2026, author listed as 'OpenAI'), claims the Gaussian moat conjecture in a uniform form. Its Theorem 'Uniform component bound' (main.tex) says: for every finite real D there is a finite B_D such that every connected component of the graph G_D has at most B_D vertices. G_D has all Gaussian primes as vertices, with an edge between distinct z, w when the Euclidean distance |z - w| is at most D. The bound is independent of the starting prime and includes primes on the coordinate axes. The corollary is that every sequence of distinct Gaussian primes with successive distances at most D has at most B_D terms, so no infinite such sequence exists for any D. For D < 1 the bound B_D = 1 is immediate, since distinct lattice points are then never adjacent. The argument reduces this (periodicity.tex, Proposition 'From a periodic obstruction to a uniform bound') to a finite sieve theorem (main.tex, Theorem 'Finite sieve obstruction'; its proof is at the end of information.tex). That theorem says: for each D >= 1 there is a finite set P_D of rational primes congruent to 1 mod 4 such that the set A(P_D) of Gaussian integers avoiding both chosen conjugate prime factors of each p in P_D contains no infinite self-avoiding walk with steps at most D. The proof of the sieve theorem is a contradiction argument. If an avoiding walk exists for large M, then entropy and information estimates on prime batches (geometric sampling of endpoints, a coverage-transfer theorem, a common sampling schedule with a shared terminal-time law, and a telescoping entropy budget) force a sum of per-batch information costs, each at least c_1/log T, to be at most log K_D and yet to diverge as M grows.
entries.delivers: If the claim holds, it answers the bullet negatively for the Euclidean metric and for every step bound C: no infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes with |x_{n+1} - x_n| <= C exists, from any starting prime. The manuscript's abstract says 'We prove the Gaussian moat conjecture', and its introduction says the result 'proves the uniform form of the Gaussian moat conjecture and answers the infinite-walk question negatively'. Its formulation ('whether some G_D contains an infinite path with no repeated vertex') is the list's question in graph language, so the wording matches up to notation. The claim also covers the origin-started variant, since it applies to every starting prime. Beyond the bullet, it gives a uniform bound on component sizes of G_D.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, neither part (a) nor part (b) of the bullet remains open. The manuscript does not give an explicit B_D, an explicit P_D or M, or any explicit dependence of the bound on D. The bound is stated to be nonexplicit.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture: no infinite bounded-step walk through Gaussian primes, in a uniform component-size form
entries.object: No explicit object. The obstruction is a finite set P_D of rational primes congruent to 1 mod 4, with a chosen Gaussian factor for each, defining a periodic set A(P_D) in Z[i]. It is not explicit: P_D is taken to be P_M for an unspecified sufficiently large M, which is found by contradiction. No infinite walk is constructed, since the result is a nonexistence claim.
entries.doubts: (a) The thresholds are not explicit. The constants g_0, c_0 and B and the threshold for M are only asserted to exist ('for sufficiently large M'), and uniformity over the hypothetical walks is asserted rather than quantified. (b) The argument relies on material I did not check in full: the choice of constants and the iteration in schedule.tex (I read lines 1-60 and 400-538 only), the entropy and displacement estimates behind the labelled equations smoothing, native-data, checkpoint-entropy and terminal-entropy, the geometric lemmas in geometry.tex (I read only the enrichment statement and its surrounding text), and the proof of Proposition 'Information cost of one batch' in information.tex (I read lines 1-60 and 280-417 only). (c) The schedule section states that conditioning on residue vectors 'will be treated separately' in the next section. I did not confirm that the information section fully discharges this. (d) The entropy-enrichment lemma is stated for an 'asymptotic family' with an O_D(g) error term and no explicit rates. (e) The text states the result without hedges. It is attributed to 'OpenAI' with no individual authors, and the references are all predecessors (Gethner-Stark, Gethner-Wagon-Wick, Tsuchimura, Vardi, Tao, Selberg, Lugosi, Conrad and Cover-Thomas).
